newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: MeesPierson impact immediately positive - Fortis.
newsitem.headline: MeesPierson impact immediately positive - Fortis.

text.p: Dutch-Belgian financial group Fortis said on Wednesday its recent investment banking acquisition, MeesPierson, made an immediate positive contribution to group results in the first quarter of 1997.
Fortis, jointly owned by Dutch group Fortis Amev and Belgium's Fortis AG, earlier announced a first quarter net profit of 204 million ECUs, up from 157 million a year ago.
"As expected MeesPierson immediately made a positive contribution," it said. Fortis's 2.5 billion guilder purchase of MeesPierson from ABN AMRO was effective January 1.
Fortis' 52 percent profit growth from banking outstripped that of insurance, which was up 17 percent on a year earlier.
It said operating results from the banking operations of Fortis Nederland almost quadrupled.

Fortis said the inclusion of MeesPierson meant the nature of its banking activities had changed, and this was mainly seen in the increased relative importance of net commission and the result from financial transactions.
The group also said the result from VSB Bank developed satisfactorily as a result of higher net commissions and cost control.
